at ramme.explanation: "At ramme" means "to hit" what you aim at, so you do not miss. It can also mean "to affect" someone badly: Krisen ramte mange (The crisis hit many people).

sentence.da: Kan du **ramme** målet med bolden?
sentence.en: Can you hit the target with the ball?

at ramme plet.explanation: "At ramme plet" means "to hit the mark", to be exactly right in what you say, guess or describe. Plet normally means "a spot", so the picture is hitting the middle of a target: Din beskrivelse ramte plet (Your description hit the mark).

sentence.da: Hun vil **ramme plet** med sit gæt.
sentence.en: She will hit the mark with her guess.

at rapportere.explanation: "At rapportere" means "to report", telling someone the facts: Hun rapporterer til chefen (She reports to the boss). It is also used for news: Avisen rapporterer om ulykken (The paper reports on the accident).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **rapportere** til min leder hver mandag.
sentence.en: I have to report to my manager every Monday.

at rasle.explanation: "At rasle" means "to rattle", to make a short, dry sound, like small hard things knocking together: Nøglerne rasler i lommen (The keys rattle in the pocket). It also fits dry leaves and paper, where English says "rustle": Tørre blade rasler i vinden (Dry leaves rustle in the wind).

sentence.da: Mønterne kan **rasle** i dåsen, når jeg ryster den.
sentence.en: The coins can rattle in the tin when I shake it.

at rationalisere.explanation: "At rationalisere" means "to rationalize". At work it means to make a way of working faster and cheaper by removing steps that waste time. It can also mean to find sensible-sounding reasons for something you did: Han rationaliserer sit valg (He rationalizes his choice).

sentence.da: Firmaet vil **rationalisere** produktionen for at spare penge.
sentence.en: The company wants to rationalize production in order to save money.

at reagere.explanation: "At reagere" means "to react", meaning what you do or say in response: Hun reagerede hurtigt (She reacted quickly). What you react to comes after på (to): Han reagerer på kritik (He reacts to criticism).

sentence.da: Jeg ved ikke, hvordan jeg skal **reagere**.
sentence.en: I do not know how I should react.

at realisere.explanation: "At realisere" means "to realize" in the sense of making a plan or dream real. To become aware of something, Danes say at indse (to see that something is so): Jeg indser, at jeg tog fejl (I realize that I was wrong).

sentence.da: Hun vil **realisere** sin drøm om at åbne en café.
sentence.en: She wants to realize her dream of opening a cafe.

at redde.explanation: "At redde" means "to save" or "to rescue" from danger: Han reddede barnet (He rescued the child). Saving money is different: at spare (to save money).

sentence.da: Brandmanden kan **redde** hunden fra branden.
sentence.en: The firefighter can save the dog from the fire.

at rede håret.explanation: "At rede håret" means "to comb one's hair": Hun reder håret (She combs her hair). The same verb makes a bed: at rede sengen (to make the bed).

sentence.da: Hun vil **rede håret** med en kam.
sentence.en: She wants to comb her hair with a comb.

at rede seng.explanation: "At rede seng" means "to make the bed": Han reder seng hver morgen (He makes the bed every morning). The usual verb for a bed is rede, not at lave (to make).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **rede seng**, når jeg står op.
sentence.en: I want to make the bed when I get up.

at redegøre for.explanation: "At redegøre for" means "to account for", to set out something fully and in order, such as what happened or why you chose it: redegøre for en beslutning (to account for a decision). Always add for before the thing you set out.

sentence.da: Du skal **redegøre for** pengene, og chefen vil se kvitteringerne.
sentence.en: You must account for the money, and the boss wants to see the receipts.

at redigere.explanation: "At redigere" means "to edit", to work on a text, photo, video or file to improve it. The person who decides what goes into a newspaper or a book is en redaktør (an editor).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **redigere** videoen, før jeg lægger den på nettet.
sentence.en: I have to edit the video before I put it online.

at reducere.explanation: "At reducere" means "to reduce", to make an amount, size or price smaller, often by a stated number: Prisen er reduceret med ti procent (The price is reduced by ten percent). On a sign, reduceret pris means a sale price.

sentence.da: Man kan **reducere** sit strømforbrug ved at slukke lyset.
sentence.en: You can reduce your electricity use by turning off the light.

at referere.explanation: "At referere" means "to refer" and "to report". With til (to), it points back to something already said or written: Jeg refererer til din mail (I am referring to your email). Without it, it means to retell in short what someone said or wrote: Han refererede artiklen for os (He told us what the article said).

sentence.da: Hun skal **referere** mødet for dem, der ikke var der.
sentence.en: She has to report on the meeting for those who were not there.

at reflektere.explanation: "At reflektere" means "to reflect", used for both thought and light. To think deeply about something, add over (on): Jeg reflekterer over mit valg (I am reflecting on my choice). Light bouncing off a surface needs no extra word: Sneen reflekterer lyset (The snow reflects the light).

sentence.da: Du bør **reflektere** over, hvad du har lært i dag.
sentence.en: You should reflect on what you have learned today.

at regere.explanation: "At regere" means "to govern" and "to rule", used for a king, a queen or a political party in charge of a country. For a shop or a company, say at drive (to run).

sentence.da: Hvilket parti vil **regere** landet efter valget?
sentence.en: Which party will govern the country after the election?

at registrere.explanation: "At registrere" means "to register", to write something into an official list or system: Kommunen registrerer alle borgere (The municipality registers all citizens). It also means to notice: Jeg registrerede ikke, at han gik (I did not notice that he left).

sentence.da: Du skal **registrere** din bil, før du må køre i den.
sentence.en: You have to register your car before you may drive it.

at regne.explanation: "At regne" means "to rain": Det regner (It is raining). At regne can also mean "to calculate": Han regner hurtigt (He calculates quickly).

sentence.da: I dag skal det **regne**.
sentence.en: Today it is going to rain.

at regne med.explanation: "At regne med" means "to count on", and also "to expect": Jeg regner med dig (I am counting on you). Vi regner med regn i morgen (We expect rain tomorrow).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **regne med** hjælp fra min bror.
sentence.en: I can count on help from my brother.

at rehabilitere.explanation: "At rehabilitere" means "to rehabilitate", to help someone get back their health or ability after an injury, an illness or an addiction. It is also used for a person who gets their good name back after being wrongly blamed.

sentence.da: Vi skal **rehabilitere** patienten, så han kan gå igen.
sentence.en: We must rehabilitate the patient so that he can walk again.

at rejse.explanation: "At rejse" means "to travel" or "to go away on a trip": Jeg rejser til Danmark (I am traveling to Denmark). For "have traveled", Danish uses er (am) instead of har (have): Jeg er rejst (I have left).

sentence.da: Vi vil **rejse** til Spanien i morgen.
sentence.en: We want to travel to Spain tomorrow.

at rejse sig.explanation: "At rejse sig" means "to stand up" or "to rise": Han rejste sig fra stolen (He stood up from the chair). The little word changes with the person: Jeg rejser mig (I stand up), Du rejser dig (You stand up).

sentence.da: Alle skal **rejse sig**, når læreren kommer ind.
sentence.en: Everyone has to stand up when the teacher comes in.

at rekruttere.explanation: "At rekruttere" means "to recruit", to find new people and bring them into a company, a team or the army: Hæren rekrutterer unge mænd og kvinder (The army recruits young men and women).

sentence.da: Firmaet vil **rekruttere** ti nye medarbejdere i år.
sentence.en: The company wants to recruit ten new employees this year.

at renovere.explanation: "At renovere" means "to renovate", to repair and freshen up an old house, apartment or room so that it is like new. For a single coat of paint, Danes just say at male (to paint).

sentence.da: Vi vil **renovere** badeværelset, fordi fliserne er gamle.
sentence.en: We want to renovate the bathroom because the tiles are old.

at rense.explanation: "At rense" means "to clean" by taking out dirt: Vi renser vandet (We clean the water). For cleaning a house, use at gøre rent: Jeg gør rent (I clean).

sentence.da: Du skal **rense** såret med vand.
sentence.en: You have to clean the wound with water.

at reparere.explanation: "At reparere" means "to repair" or "to fix" something broken: Hun reparerer en gammel radio (She repairs an old radio). It is the opposite of at ødelægge (to break).

sentence.da: Kan du **reparere** min cykel i dag?
sentence.en: Can you repair my bike today?

at repetere.explanation: "At repetere" means "to review", to go over something you have studied before so that it stays in your head. It does not mean to say something again. For that, use at gentage (to repeat).

sentence.da: Før prøven skal jeg **repetere** alle ordene fra i år.
sentence.en: Before the test I have to review all the words from this year.

at repræsentere.explanation: "At repræsentere" means "to represent", to speak or act for a group, a country or a company: Hun repræsenterer Danmark ved OL (She represents Denmark at the Olympics). It also means to stand for an idea: Flaget repræsenterer frihed (The flag stands for freedom).

sentence.da: Han skal **repræsentere** hele klassen ved mødet i morgen.
sentence.en: He is going to represent the whole class at the meeting tomorrow.

at reservere.explanation: "At reservere" means "to reserve", for a table, a room or a seat: Jeg vil gerne reservere en plads (I would like to reserve a seat). At booke (to book) means nearly the same.

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **reservere** et bord i aften.
sentence.en: I would like to reserve a table tonight.

at respektere.explanation: "At respektere" means "to respect" a person, and also "to accept" something such as a rule or a choice: Vi respekterer reglerne (We respect the rules).

sentence.da: Du skal **respektere** andre menneskers valg.
sentence.en: You have to respect other people's choices.

at respondere.explanation: "At respondere" means "to respond", to answer or get back to a message, a request or a signal. In everyday talk, Danes mostly say at svare (to answer). Respondere fits machines and systems well: Appen responderer ikke (The app is not responding).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **respondere**, før jeg har læst mailen.
sentence.en: I cannot respond before I have read the email.

at restaurere.explanation: "At restaurere" means "to restore", to put something old back the way it once looked, like a painting, a church or an old car. For a computer file, Danes say at gendanne (to bring back).

sentence.da: Han bruger mange år på at **restaurere** gamle møbler.
sentence.en: He spends many years restoring old furniture.

at retfærdiggøre.explanation: "At retfærdiggøre" means "to justify", to show that something is right or reasonable, often an action that people question: Intet kan retfærdiggøre vold (Nothing can justify violence). It is built from retfærdig (fair) and gøre (to make).

sentence.da: Han prøver at **retfærdiggøre** sit valg, men ingen tror på ham.
sentence.en: He tries to justify his choice, but nobody believes him.

at rette.explanation: "At rette" means "to correct": Kan du rette fejlen i teksten? (Can you correct the mistake in the text?) It also means "to straighten": Hun rettede ryggen (She straightened her back).

sentence.da: Læreren skal **rette** vores prøver i aften.
sentence.en: The teacher has to correct our tests tonight.

at returnere.explanation: "At returnere" means "to return an item", for example to a store: Jeg vil returnere kjolen (I want to return the dress). For coming back yourself, use at vende tilbage (to come back).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **returnere** jakken, fordi den er for stor.
sentence.en: I want to return the jacket because it is too big.

at ride.explanation: "At ride" means "to ride (a horse)": Hun rider hver weekend (She rides every weekend). For a bike, say at cykle (to cycle): Jeg cykler på arbejde (I cycle to work).

sentence.da: Hun kan **ride** på hesten i skoven.
sentence.en: She can ride the horse in the forest.

at ringe.explanation: "At ringe" means "to call" someone on the phone. You put til (to) before the person: Jeg ringer til dig i morgen (I will call you tomorrow). It also means "to ring", like a bell or a doorbell: Klokken ringer (The bell is ringing).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ringe** til min mor.
sentence.en: I want to call my mother.

at ringe efter.explanation: "At ringe efter" means "to call for" someone or something to come: Vi ringer efter en taxa (We call a taxi). To phone a person, use til: Jeg ringer til Anna (I call Anna).

sentence.da: Vi må **ringe efter** en læge nu.
sentence.en: We have to call for a doctor now.

at ringe op.explanation: "At ringe op" means "to call" someone on the phone. Put the person between ringe and op: Jeg ringer dig op (I call you). It means the same as ringe til (to call): Jeg ringer til dig (I call you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ringe op** og bestille en pizza.
sentence.en: I want to call and order a pizza.

at ringe på.explanation: "At ringe på" means "to ring the doorbell": Der ringer nogen på (Someone is ringing the doorbell). To call someone by phone, use at ringe til (to call): Jeg ringer til dig (I call you).

sentence.da: Du kan **ringe på**, hvis døren er låst.
sentence.en: You can ring the doorbell if the door is locked.

at ringe til.explanation: "At ringe til" means "to call" someone on the phone. You need til (to) before the person: Jeg ringer til min mor (I call my mother). At ringe on its own can also mean a bell ringing: Klokken ringer (The bell is ringing).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ringe til** min mor.
sentence.en: I want to call my mother.

at ringe tilbage.explanation: "At ringe tilbage" means "to call back", to return a call you missed: Jeg ringer tilbage om en time (I will call back in an hour).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ringe tilbage**, når jeg er hjemme.
sentence.en: I will call back when I am home.

at risikere.explanation: "At risikere" means "to risk", doing something where a bad result may follow: Han risikerer sit job (He is risking his job). It also means "to run the chance of" something bad, often with at: Du risikerer at blive syg (You risk getting sick).

sentence.da: Du kan **risikere** at komme for sent.
sentence.en: You might end up being late.

at riste.explanation: "At riste" means "to toast" and "to roast", to heat food dry until it turns brown and crisp, such as bread, nuts, seeds and coffee beans. Do not mix it up with at ryste (to shake), which looks almost the same.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **riste** nødderne på en tør pande.
sentence.en: I want to toast the nuts in a dry pan.

at rive.explanation: "At rive" means "to grate" food like cheese or carrots on a grater. It also means "to rake" leaves together: Han river bladene sammen (He rakes the leaves together).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **rive** ost til pastaen.
sentence.en: I have to grate cheese for the pasta.

at rive i stykker.explanation: "At rive i stykker" means "to tear to pieces": Jeg river brevet i stykker (I tear the letter to pieces). I stykker (in pieces) shows that the thing ends up in bits.

sentence.da: Hunden plejer at **rive i stykker** gamle sko.
sentence.en: The dog usually tears old shoes to pieces.

at rive ned.explanation: "At rive ned" means "to tear down", mostly a building or a wall: De river det gamle hus ned (They are tearing down the old house). With a short word like det (it), that word goes before ned: De river det ned (They are tearing it down).

sentence.da: De vil **rive ned** det gamle hus.
sentence.en: They want to tear down the old house.

at ro.explanation: "At ro" means "to row" a boat with oars: Hun roer hver morgen (She rows every morning). Look-alike: the noun ro means "calm" or "quiet": Jeg vil have lidt ro (I want some peace and quiet).

sentence.da: Vi kan **ro** over søen i en lille båd.
sentence.en: We can row across the lake in a small boat.

at rode.explanation: "At rode" means "to rummage" and "to mess up". To rummage is to search through things carelessly: Jeg roder i skuffen efter en pen (I am rummaging in the drawer for a pen). To mess up is to leave a place untidy: Børnene har rodet i stuen (The children have made a mess in the living room).

sentence.da: Han må **rode** i tasken for at finde sine nøgler.
sentence.en: He has to rummage in the bag to find his keys.

at rose.explanation: "At rose" means "to praise" and is the opposite of criticizing: Læreren roser eleven (The teacher praises the student). It looks like en rose (a rose), but this one is a word for saying good things.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **rose** dig for dit arbejde.
sentence.en: I want to praise you for your work.

at rulle.explanation: "At rulle" means "to roll", to move by turning over and over. You can also roll something yourself: Jeg ruller dejen (I roll the dough).

sentence.da: Bolden kan **rulle** ned ad bakken.
sentence.en: The ball can roll down the hill.

at runde af.explanation: "At runde af" means "to round off". For numbers: Jeg runder 4,6 af til 5 (I round 4.6 off to 5). For an event: Vi rundede aftenen af med kaffe (We rounded off the evening with coffee).

sentence.da: Vi vil **runde af** med en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: We want to round off with a cup of coffee.

at runde ned.explanation: "At runde ned" means "to round down" a number: Vi runder 7,2 ned til 7 (We round 7.2 down to 7). Ned (down) shows the direction, as in at skrive ned (to write down).

sentence.da: Prisen er 52 kroner, men vi kan **runde ned** til 50.
sentence.en: The price is 52 kroner, but we can round down to 50.

at runde op.explanation: "At runde op" means "to round up", to change a number to the next higher round number. Here op means "up", as in at ringe op (to call up) and at tage op (to pick up). The opposite is at runde ned (to round down).

sentence.da: Du kan **runde op** til nærmeste hundrede.
sentence.en: You can round up to the nearest hundred.

at rydde.explanation: "At rydde" means "to clear": Jeg rydder bordet (I clear the table). With op it means "to tidy up": Børnene rydder op (The children tidy up).

sentence.da: Efter maden skal vi **rydde** bordet.
sentence.en: After the meal we have to clear the table.

at rydde op.explanation: "At rydde op" means "to tidy up": Jeg rydder op i stuen (I tidy up the living room). It is built from at rydde (to clear) and op (up), and rydde works alone too: at rydde bordet (to clear the table).

sentence.da: Du skal **rydde op** på dit værelse nu.
sentence.en: You have to tidy up your room now.

at ryge.explanation: "At ryge" means "to smoke": Jeg ryger ikke (I do not smoke). The smoke itself is røg: Der er røg i køkkenet (There is smoke in the kitchen).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne holde op med at **ryge**.
sentence.en: He would like to quit smoking.

at rykke.explanation: "At rykke" means "to move" and "to pull". To move is to shift a short way to a new place: Vi rykker tættere sammen (We move closer together). To pull is to give a quick, hard tug: Hun rykkede i snoren (She tugged the cord).

sentence.da: Kan I **rykke** lidt, så der er plads til mig?
sentence.en: Can you move over a bit so there is room for me?

at rynke.explanation: "At rynke" means "to wrinkle", to make small lines in cloth, paper or skin. With the forehead it means to frown: Hun rynkede panden (She frowned).

sentence.da: Skjorten vil **rynke**, hvis du propper den ned i kufferten.
sentence.en: The shirt will wrinkle if you stuff it into the suitcase.

at ryste.explanation: "At ryste" means "to shake": Jeg ryster af kulde (I am shaking from the cold). You can shake something too, such as a drink: Hun ryster en drink (She shakes a drink).

sentence.da: Du skal **ryste** flasken før brug.
sentence.en: You have to shake the bottle before use.

at ryste på hovedet.explanation: "At ryste på hovedet" means "to shake one's head", a sign of no, or of disbelief or disapproval. To say what you shook your head at, use af: Jeg rystede på hovedet af hans svar (I shook my head at his answer).

sentence.da: Hun kunne kun **ryste på hovedet**, da hun hørte prisen.
sentence.en: She could only shake her head when she heard the price.

at råbe.explanation: "At råbe" means "to shout": Han råber ad mig (He is yelling at me). To call out for something, use på: Jeg råbte på hjælp (I shouted for help).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **råbe** så højt herinde.
sentence.en: You must not shout so loudly in here.

at råde over.explanation: "At råde over" means "to have at your disposal", to own or control something you can use: råde over en bil (to have a car at your disposal). Without over, at råde means "to advise": Jeg råder dig til at vente (I advise you to wait).

forms.en: I have had at my disposal

sentence.da: Skolen kan **råde over** en stor sal til festen.
sentence.en: The school can have a big hall at its disposal for the party.

at rådføre sig.explanation: "At rådføre sig" means "to consult", to ask an expert or someone experienced for advice before you decide. The other person comes after med, and sig changes with the person: Jeg rådfører mig med lægen (I consult the doctor).

sentence.da: Hun vil **rådføre sig** med en advokat og læse kontrakten først.
sentence.en: She will consult a lawyer and read the contract first.

at rådne.explanation: "At rådne" means "to rot", to slowly break down and go bad, like fruit left out too long or leaves on the ground. Milk is different: it bliver sur (becomes sour).

sentence.da: Træet vil **rådne**, hvis det står ude i regnen hele vinteren.
sentence.en: The wood will rot if it stands outside in the rain all winter.

at række.explanation: "At række" means "to reach" and "to hand": Kan du række mig saltet? (Can you hand me the salt?) It also means "to be enough": Pengene rækker ikke (The money is not enough).

sentence.da: Kan du **række** mig en kop, tak?
sentence.en: Can you hand me a cup, please?

at række hånden op.explanation: "At række hånden op" means "to raise one's hand". Danish says the hand (hånden), not my hand. Op (up) shows the hand going up.

sentence.da: Hun vil **række hånden op**, når hun kender svaret.
sentence.en: She wants to raise her hand when she knows the answer.

at rødme.explanation: "At rødme" means "to blush", when your face turns red from a strong feeling such as shyness or embarrassment, often after praise or a slip in front of others. Being rød i hovedet (red in the face) can also come from effort or anger, but rødme is mostly about shyness and embarrassment.

sentence.da: Han plejer at **rødme**, når nogen roser ham foran andre.
sentence.en: He usually blushes when someone praises him in front of others.

at røre.explanation: "At røre" means "to touch", and also "to stir": Rør i suppen (Stir the soup). To touch something, add ved: Du må ikke røre ved den (You must not touch it).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **røre** ved ovnen, fordi den er varm.
sentence.en: You must not touch the oven, because it is hot.

at røre rundt.explanation: "At røre rundt" means "to stir", moving a spoon around in a pot. Rundt means "around", and it works with other verbs too: at gå rundt (to walk around), at køre rundt (to drive around).

sentence.da: Du skal **røre rundt** i gryden hele tiden.
sentence.en: You have to stir the pot all the time.

at røve.explanation: "At røve" means "to rob", to take things from a person or place by force or threat. When nobody is threatened, use at stjæle (to steal).

sentence.da: Tre mænd prøvede at **røve** banken, men blev fanget.
sentence.en: Three men tried to rob the bank but were caught.

en rabat.explanation: "En rabat" means "a discount", an amount taken off the price. You can ask Kan jeg få rabat? (Can I get a discount?), with no en in front of rabat.

sentence.da: Butikken giver mig **rabat** på en jakke.
sentence.en: The store gives me a discount on a jacket.

en race.explanation: "En race" means "a breed", a type of animal with its own looks, such as en hunderace (a dog breed). A running race is et løb, not en race.

sentence.da: Labrador er en **race**, som mange bruger som førerhund.
sentence.en: Labrador is a breed that many use as a guide dog.

en radar.explanation: "En radar" means "a radar", a device that finds planes or ships far away using radio waves.

sentence.da: Skibet kan se andre skibe på sin **radar**.
sentence.en: The ship can see other ships on its radar.

en radiator.explanation: "En radiator" means "a radiator", the heater on the wall. To turn it up, say skrue op (turn up). Op adds the idea of going up, so it also works for sound: skrue op for lyden (turn up the sound).

sentence.da: Der er en **radiator** under vinduet, og den er varm.
sentence.en: There is a radiator under the window, and it is warm.

en radio.explanation: "En radio" means "a radio". Danish says i radioen (literally in the radio) where English says on the radio, as in Det var i radioen (It was on the radio).

sentence.da: Jeg hører **radio** og musik i bilen.
sentence.en: I listen to the radio and music in the car.

en radioavis.explanation: "En radioavis" means "a radio news broadcast". It is built from radio (radio) and en avis (a newspaper), as if the paper were read out on the radio. On its own, en avis is the printed paper: Jeg læser avisen (I read the paper).

sentence.da: I en **radioavis** hører man nyheder.
sentence.en: In a radio news broadcast you hear the news.

en radius.explanation: "En radius" means "a radius", the distance from the middle of a circle to its edge. It is also used for the space around a place: Alle butikker inden for en radius af to kilometer (All shops within a radius of two kilometers).

sentence.da: Hvis **radius** er fem centimeter, er cirklen ti centimeter bred.
sentence.en: If the radius is five centimeters, the circle is ten centimeters wide.

en raket.explanation: "En raket" means "a rocket", a tube-shaped vehicle that flies into space, or a firework you shoot into the sky.

sentence.da: En **raket** bruger brændstof til at flyve helt op i rummet.
sentence.en: A rocket uses fuel to fly all the way up into space.

en rang.explanation: "En rang" means "a rank", a person's level in a system with many levels, such as the army. A person high up is called af høj rang (of high rank).

sentence.da: Soldaten fik en højere **rang**, efter at han havde reddet holdet.
sentence.en: The soldier got a higher rank after he had saved the team.

en rangorden.explanation: "En rangorden" means "a ranking", a fixed ladder of who or what stands higher and lower, in status or importance. It is often used about a social group where everyone knows who is above whom.

sentence.da: Hos hønsene er der en fast **rangorden**.
sentence.en: Among the hens there is a fixed ranking.

en rapport.explanation: "En rapport" means "a report", a written document about work or results.

sentence.da: Jeg skal aflevere min **rapport** i morgen.
sentence.en: I have to hand in my report tomorrow.

en reaktion.explanation: "En reaktion" means "a reaction", how someone or something responds. To say what was reacted to, use på: en reaktion på nyheden (a reaction to the news).

sentence.da: Hans **reaktion** var meget rolig.
sentence.en: His reaction was very calm.

en recept.explanation: "En recept" means "a prescription", the note from a doctor that you take to the pharmacy to get medicine. It does not mean a cooking recipe: that is en opskrift (a recipe).

sentence.da: Lægen giver mig en **recept** til apoteket.
sentence.en: The doctor gives me a prescription for the pharmacy.

en reception.explanation: "En reception" means "a reception desk", the front desk of a hotel or an office. The person who works there is en receptionist (a receptionist).

sentence.da: Hotellet har en **reception**, og den er åben hele natten.
sentence.en: The hotel has a front desk, and it is open all night.

en receptionist.explanation: "En receptionist" means "a receptionist", the person at the entrance of a hotel or office who welcomes people and answers the phone.

sentence.da: På hotellet hjælper en **receptionist** gæsterne med at tjekke ind.
sentence.en: At the hotel a receptionist helps the guests check in.

en recession.explanation: "En recession" means "a recession", a time when a country's economy shrinks for some months in a row and companies earn less.

sentence.da: Under en **recession** køber folk mindre, så flere firmaer lukker.
sentence.en: During a recession people buy less, so more firms close.

en redaktion.explanation: "En redaktion" means "an editorial office", the place and the team where articles and news shows are put together. It can also mean just the staff who decide what gets published.

sentence.da: På en **redaktion** skriver og vælger man nyheder til avisen.
sentence.en: At an editorial office, people write and choose the news for the paper.

en redaktør.explanation: "En redaktør" means "an editor", the person who decides what is published and checks the texts before they go out. Many newspapers and magazines have one in charge: en chefredaktør (an editor in chief).

sentence.da: Hun er **redaktør** og læser alle artikler, før de udkommer.
sentence.en: She is an editor and reads all articles before they come out.

en rede.explanation: "En rede" means "a nest", the home a bird builds to raise its young. Some insects and other animals make one too.

sentence.da: Fuglen har lagt tre æg i sin **rede**.
sentence.en: The bird has laid three eggs in its nest.

en redegørelse.explanation: "En redegørelse" means "an account" or "a report", a clear and detailed statement of what happened or how things stand. It is often official or written. It belongs to at redegøre for (to account for).

sentence.da: Direktøren skrev en **redegørelse** om ulykken.
sentence.en: The director wrote a report about the accident.

en redning.explanation: "En redning" means "a rescue", when someone is brought out of danger. It also works for a lucky break: Det var redningen! (That was just what we needed!)

sentence.da: Politiets **redning** af drengen fra isen tog en time.
sentence.en: The police's rescue of the boy from the ice took an hour.

en redningskrans.explanation: "En redningskrans" means "a lifebuoy", a ring that floats and is thrown to someone in the water. It is built from en krans (a ring) and redning (rescue). Krans also means a wreath, as in en julekrans (a Christmas wreath).

sentence.da: Han kastede en **redningskrans** ud til manden i vandet.
sentence.en: He threw a lifebuoy out to the man in the water.

en redningsvest.explanation: "En redningsvest" means "a life jacket", a vest that keeps you afloat in water. It is built from redning (rescue) and vest (vest). Vest also means west: Vi kører mod vest (We drive west).

sentence.da: Alle børn skal have **redningsvest** på i båden.
sentence.en: All children must wear a life jacket in the boat.

en reform.explanation: "En reform" means "a reform", a big change to how a part of society is run, decided by politicians: en skolereform (a school reform).

sentence.da: Politikerne vil gøre skolen bedre med en stor **reform**.
sentence.en: The politicians want to make school better with a big reform.

en regel.explanation: "En regel" means "a rule". Som regel (as a rule) means "usually": Som regel venter jeg (I usually wait).

sentence.da: Der er en **regel** om at vente her.
sentence.en: There is a rule about waiting here.

en regering.explanation: "En regering" means "a government", the group of leaders who run a country.

sentence.da: Den nye **regering** vil bygge flere skoler.
sentence.en: The new government wants to build more schools.

en region.explanation: "En region" means "a region", a large part of a country: Danmark har fem regioner (Denmark has five regions).

sentence.da: Hver **region** i Danmark har sine egne sygehuse.
sentence.en: Each region in Denmark has its own hospitals.

en regnbue.explanation: "En regnbue" means "a rainbow", the colored arc in the sky when the sun shines through rain. It is built from regn (rain) and bue (arc). Bue also means a bow, as in pil og bue (bow and arrow).

sentence.da: Solen og regnen laver en **regnbue** på himlen.
sentence.en: The sun and the rain make a rainbow in the sky.

en regnbyge.explanation: "En regnbyge" means "a rain shower", a short burst of rain that soon passes. It is built from regn (rain) and byge (shower). Byge is also in en snebyge (a snow shower).

sentence.da: Vi blev våde i en kort **regnbyge**.
sentence.en: We got wet in a short rain shower.

en regning.explanation: "En regning" means "a bill", at a restaurant or at home, for example for electricity. In a restaurant, you can ask politely Må jeg bede om regningen? (May I ask for the bill?).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler en **regning** for strøm.
sentence.en: I pay a bill for electricity.

en regnjakke.explanation: "En regnjakke" means "a rain jacket", a waterproof jacket that keeps you dry. It is made of regn (rain) and jakke (jacket).

sentence.da: Jeg tager min **regnjakke** på i regnen.
sentence.en: I put my rain jacket on in the rain.

en regnskov.explanation: "En regnskov" means "a rainforest", a thick forest in a warm place such as the Amazon. Amazonas er verdens største regnskov (The Amazon is the world's largest rainforest).

sentence.da: Det regner hele året i en **regnskov**.
sentence.en: It rains all year in a rainforest.

en regnvejrsdag.explanation: "En regnvejrsdag" means "a rainy day", a day for staying inside: På en regnvejrsdag bliver vi hjemme (On a rainy day we stay home). It is built from regnvejr (a spell of rain) and dag (day).

sentence.da: Det regner i dag, og det er en rigtig **regnvejrsdag**.
sentence.en: It is raining today, and it is a real rainy day.

en regulering.explanation: "En regulering" means "a regulation" and "an adjustment". It can be the act of setting something to the right level, like en regulering af varmen (an adjustment of the heat), or official limits set by the authorities for an area.

sentence.da: Staten har indført en **regulering** af huslejen.
sentence.en: The state has introduced a regulation of rents.

en reje.explanation: "En reje" means "a shrimp", also called a prawn. Rejemad (shrimp on bread) is made of reje (shrimp) and mad (food).

sentence.da: En **reje** er et lille dyr i havet.
sentence.en: A shrimp is a small animal in the sea.

en rejemad.explanation: "En rejemad" means "a shrimp open sandwich", a Danish lunch classic eaten with a knife and fork. Mad alone means food, but in a word like this it is a slice of bread with a topping.

sentence.da: En **rejemad** er brød med rejer, mayonnaise og citron.
sentence.en: A shrimp open sandwich is bread with shrimp, mayonnaise and lemon.

en rejse.explanation: "En rejse" means "a trip" or "a journey", usually a longer one such as a vacation abroad. For a short outing, Danes say en tur (a trip, a walk). You can wish someone a good journey with God rejse! (Have a good trip!).

sentence.da: Vi tager på en lang **rejse** til Spanien.
sentence.en: We are going on a long trip to Spain.

en rejseforsikring.explanation: "En rejseforsikring" means "a travel insurance policy", which pays if something goes wrong on a trip, like illness or lost bags.

sentence.da: Hvis jeg bliver syg, betaler min **rejseforsikring**.
sentence.en: If I get sick, my travel insurance pays.

en rejsende.explanation: "En rejsende" means "a traveler", a person who is on a trip. It comes from at rejse (to travel).

sentence.da: Alle **rejsende** skal vise deres pas.
sentence.en: All travelers have to show their passports.

en rejseplan.explanation: "En rejseplan" means "an itinerary", a plan with the places and times of a trip. For a bus or train timetable, use en køreplan (a timetable).

sentence.da: Min **rejseplan** viser hotellet og flyet.
sentence.en: My itinerary shows the hotel and the flight.

en reklamation.explanation: "En reklamation" means "a complaint (faulty item)", when you tell a shop that something you bought is not as it should be. The matching action is at reklamere (to make a claim).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver en **reklamation**, fordi telefonen er gået i stykker.
sentence.en: I am writing a complaint because the phone has broken.

en reklame.explanation: "En reklame" means "an advertisement" and also "a commercial" on TV. To advertise is at reklamere.

sentence.da: Der var en lang **reklame** midt i filmen.
sentence.en: There was a long commercial in the middle of the movie.

en rekord.explanation: "En rekord" means "a record", the best result ever reached in a sport or contest. A music record is en plade.

sentence.da: Hun satte ny **rekord** i svømning i går.
sentence.en: She set a new record in swimming yesterday.

en rektor.explanation: "En rektor" means "a principal", the head of a high school. At a university the head is called rektor too.

sentence.da: Skolens **rektor** er chef for alle lærerne.
sentence.en: The school's principal is the boss of all the teachers.

en religion.explanation: "En religion" means "a religion", a set of beliefs about God or the meaning of life, with its own customs and holy places.

sentence.da: Kristendom er en **religion**, og islam er en anden.
sentence.en: Christianity is a religion, and Islam is another.

en ren.explanation: "En ren" means "a reindeer". Without en, the same spelling ren is the word for clean, so the en tells you which one it is.

sentence.da: En **ren** har store gevirer og lever i det kolde nord.
sentence.en: A reindeer has big antlers and lives in the cold north.

en rengøring.explanation: "En rengøring" means "a cleaning". Without en, rengøring is the general word for housecleaning: Rengøring tager lang tid (Cleaning takes a long time). It is built from at gøre rent (to clean).

sentence.da: Jeg hader **rengøring**, men huset skal være rent.
sentence.en: I hate cleaning, but the house has to be clean.

en rengøringsassistent.explanation: "En rengøringsassistent" means "a cleaner", someone whose job is keeping offices, schools and homes spotless. It is the usual job title, built from rengøring (cleaning) and assistent (assistant).

sentence.da: En **rengøringsassistent** gør kontorerne rene hver aften.
sentence.en: A cleaner cleans the offices every evening.

en renovering.explanation: "En renovering" means "a renovation", when an old building or room is repaired and made modern again, for example the kitchen or the roof. It is not used for a newly built house.

sentence.da: Huset fik nyt tag og nye vinduer ved en **renovering**.
sentence.en: The house got a new roof and new windows in a renovation.

en rente.explanation: "En rente" means "an interest rate", the percentage you pay for borrowing money or get for saving it. The word also covers plain interest: at betale rente (to pay interest).

sentence.da: Banken tager en høj **rente**, når man låner penge.
sentence.en: The bank charges a high interest rate when you borrow money.

en rentestigning.explanation: "En rentestigning" means "an interest rate rise", when borrowing gets more expensive because the rate goes up. It is built from rente (interest) and stigning (a rise), the same pattern as en prisstigning (a price rise).

sentence.da: En **rentestigning** gør det dyrere at betale sit lån tilbage.
sentence.en: An interest rate rise makes it more expensive to pay your loan back.

en reol.explanation: "En reol" means "a bookshelf", a tall piece of furniture with shelves. A single shelf is en hylde.

sentence.da: Der står mange bøger i min **reol**.
sentence.en: There are many books on my bookshelf.

en reparation.explanation: "En reparation" means "a repair", the work of fixing something that is broken. The action is at reparere (to repair).

sentence.da: Der er brug for en **reparation** af taget.
sentence.en: The roof needs a repair.

en replik.explanation: "En replik" means "a line" that an actor speaks in a play or film, and also "a retort", a quick, often sharp comeback in a conversation.

sentence.da: På scenen skal skuespilleren huske sin **replik**.
sentence.en: On stage, the actor has to remember his line.

en repræsentant.explanation: "En repræsentant" means "a representative", someone who speaks or acts for a group, a company or a country. It is often used with for: en repræsentant for firmaet (a representative of the company).

sentence.da: Hver klasse vælger en **repræsentant** til elevrådet.
sentence.en: Each class chooses a representative for the student council.

en reservation.explanation: "En reservation" means "a reservation", for example for a table, a train seat or a hotel room. To book a table, say at bestille bord (to book a table).

sentence.da: Vi har en **reservation** på restauranten i aften.
sentence.en: We have a reservation at the restaurant tonight.

en reservedel.explanation: "En reservedel" means "a spare part", a part you keep or buy to replace a broken one. It is reserve (spare) plus del (part).

sentence.da: Når cyklen går i stykker, skal jeg købe en **reservedel**.
sentence.en: When the bike breaks, I have to buy a spare part.

en ressource.explanation: "En ressource" means "a resource", something useful you can draw on, such as money, time, people or energy. The plural is common: naturlige ressourcer (natural resources).

sentence.da: Vand er en vigtig **ressource**, som vi skal passe på.
sentence.en: Water is an important resource that we must take care of.

en rest.explanation: "En rest" means "a remainder" or "a leftover". It does not mean resting. To rest, say at hvile sig (to rest).

sentence.da: Der er en **rest** pizza i køleskabet.
sentence.en: There is some leftover pizza in the fridge.

en restaurant.explanation: "En restaurant" means "a restaurant", a place where you sit down and have a meal. To say you eat out, Danes say at spise på restaurant (to eat at a restaurant), with no en after på.

sentence.da: Vi spiser på **restaurant** i aften.
sentence.en: We are eating at a restaurant tonight.

en restaurantgæst.explanation: "En restaurantgæst" means "a restaurant guest", a person who eats at a restaurant. The part gæst (guest) works in other words too: en hotelgæst (a hotel guest).

sentence.da: En **restaurantgæst** bestiller mad og betaler bagefter.
sentence.en: A restaurant guest orders food and pays afterwards.

en ret.explanation: "En ret" means "a right" and also "a dish". Vi har ret til ferie (We have a right to vacation). With have, it means being correct: Du har ret (You are right).

sentence.da: Dagens **ret** er fisk med kartofler.
sentence.en: Today's dish is fish with potatoes.

en retning.explanation: "En retning" means "a direction", the way something points or moves. To ask, say Hvilken retning? (Which direction?).

sentence.da: Bussen kører i den rigtige **retning**.
sentence.en: The bus is going in the right direction.

en retssag.explanation: "En retssag" means "a court case", a dispute that is decided in a court. It is built from ret (court) and sag (case). Ret also means dish and right, so the meaning depends on the word it sits in.

sentence.da: Ved en **retssag** afgør en dommer, hvem der har ret.
sentence.en: In a court case, a judge decides who is right.

en retsstat.explanation: "En retsstat" means "a state governed by law", a country where everyone, including the government, must follow the same rules and judges are independent.

sentence.da: I en **retsstat** gælder reglerne for alle, også for politikere.
sentence.en: In a state governed by law, the rules apply to everyone, including politicians.

en rettelse.explanation: "En rettelse" means "a correction", a fix for something wrong in a text, a number or a bill. The verb at rette also means to mark homework: Læreren retter opgaverne (The teacher marks the assignments).

sentence.da: Vi sender en **rettelse**, fordi der er en stavefejl i teksten.
sentence.en: We are sending a correction because there is a spelling mistake in the text.

en rettighed.explanation: "En rettighed" means "a right", something you are allowed to have or do by law or by agreement. You can also say ret til (right to): Du har ret til ferie (You have a right to vacation).

sentence.da: At gå i skole er en **rettighed** for alle børn.
sentence.en: Going to school is a right for all children.

en returbillet.explanation: "En returbillet" means "a round-trip ticket", one that takes you there and back. At a counter you can say En returbillet til Aarhus, tak. (A round-trip ticket to Aarhus, please.)

sentence.da: Jeg køber en **returbillet** til Aarhus og hjem.
sentence.en: I buy a round-trip ticket to Aarhus and back home.

en returnering.explanation: "En returnering" means "a return", when you send something you bought back to the shop. It is only for goods. For going back to a place, say at vende tilbage (to go back).

sentence.da: Ved **returnering** af varen får du pengene tilbage.
sentence.en: When you return the item, you get your money back.

en returret.explanation: "En returret" means "a right of return", the shop's promise that you may bring something back within a set number of days.

sentence.da: Butikken giver os **returret** i tredive dage.
sentence.en: The shop gives us a right of return for thirty days.

en revisor.explanation: "En revisor" means "an auditor", a professional who checks that a company's money and records are correct. The person who keeps the books day to day is a bogholder (bookkeeper).

sentence.da: Firmaets **revisor** gennemgår tallene hvert år.
sentence.en: The company's auditor goes through the numbers every year.

en revne.explanation: "En revne" means "a crack", a thin line where something like glass, a wall or ice has split. A sprække (a gap) is a wider opening that you can look or reach through.

sentence.da: Glasset er ikke gået i stykker, men der er en **revne**.
sentence.en: The glass has not broken, but there is a crack.

en revolution.explanation: "En revolution" means "a revolution", when people overthrow their rulers or when things change completely.

sentence.da: Folket startede en **revolution** mod kongen.
sentence.en: The people started a revolution against the king.

en revolver.explanation: "En revolver" means "a revolver", a small gun that holds bullets in a turning drum. It is much smaller than et gevær (a rifle).

sentence.da: Betjenten har en **revolver** i bæltet.
sentence.en: The officer has a revolver on his belt.

en ridder.explanation: "En ridder" means "a knight", a medieval warrior on horseback in armor. It is also an honor in Denmark: Ridder af Dannebrog (Knight of the Dannebrog order).

sentence.da: I middelalderen red en **ridder** ud for at kæmpe for kongen.
sentence.en: In the Middle Ages, a knight rode out to fight for the king.

en ridse.explanation: "En ridse" means "a scratch", a thin mark on a surface. For a scratch on skin, you can also say en rift (a scratch).

sentence.da: Der er en **ridse** på bilens dør.
sentence.en: There is a scratch on the car door.

en ring.explanation: "En ring" means "a ring" for the finger. It looks like at ringe (to call): Jeg ringer til dig (I will call you).

sentence.da: Hun har en **ring** på fingeren.
sentence.en: She has a ring on her finger.

en risalamande.explanation: "En risalamande" means "a Danish rice pudding with almonds", a cold rice pudding with whipped cream, eaten at Christmas. One whole almond is hidden in it, and the person who finds it wins a small gift.

sentence.da: Til jul spiser vi **risalamande** med varm kirsebærsovs.
sentence.en: At Christmas, we eat risalamande with warm cherry sauce.

en risiko.explanation: "En risiko" means "a risk", the possibility that something bad happens. To accept one, say at tage en risiko (to take a risk).

sentence.da: Der er en **risiko** for regn i morgen.
sentence.en: There is a risk of rain tomorrow.

en rive.explanation: "En rive" means "a rake", the garden tool for gathering leaves. The word at rive (to grate) looks the same, so the rest of the sentence tells you which one it is.

sentence.da: Jeg samler bladene med en **rive**.
sentence.en: I gather the leaves with a rake.

en robot.explanation: "En robot" means "a robot", a machine that does tasks on its own.

sentence.da: Min **robot** støvsuger gulvet hver dag.
sentence.en: My robot vacuums the floor every day.

en robåd.explanation: "En robåd" means "a rowboat", a small boat you move with oars. It is built from ro (to row) and båd (boat).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **robåd** ud på søen.
sentence.en: We take a rowboat out on the lake.

en rod.explanation: "En rod" means "a root", the part of a plant under the ground: Træet har lange rødder (The tree has long roots). Do not mix it up with et rod (a mess), which takes et: Der er rod i stuen (The living room is a mess).

sentence.da: Hver plante har en **rod** under jorden.
sentence.en: Every plant has a root under the ground.

en rolle.explanation: "En rolle" means "a role", a part an actor plays: Hun spiller en rolle i et teaterstykke (She plays a role in a play). It also means the part someone has in a group: Han har en vigtig rolle (He has an important role).

sentence.da: Hun fik en stor **rolle** i filmen.
sentence.en: She got a big role in the movie.

en roman.explanation: "En roman" means "a novel", a long made-up story: Jeg læser en spændende roman (I am reading an exciting novel). For anything from ancient Rome, say romersk (Roman): romerske tal (Roman numerals).

sentence.da: Forfatteren har skrevet en **roman** om krigen.
sentence.en: The author has written a novel about the war.

en romkugle.explanation: "En romkugle" means "a rum ball", a small round chocolate sweet with a rum flavor.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **romkugle**, og den smager af rom.
sentence.en: I eat a rum ball and it tastes of rum.

en rose.explanation: "En rose" means "a rose", the flower. A bunch of roses is en buket roser (a bouquet of roses).

sentence.da: En **rose** har torne og dufter godt.
sentence.en: A rose has thorns and smells good.

en rosin.explanation: "En rosin" means "a raisin", a dried grape. A grape is en vindrue.

sentence.da: En **rosin** er lille, sød og tør.
sentence.en: A raisin is small, sweet and dry.

en rotte.explanation: "En rotte" means "a rat". A smaller animal is en mus (a mouse).

sentence.da: Katten jagter en **rotte** i laden.
sentence.en: The cat chases a rat in the barn.

en router.explanation: "En router" means "a router", the box at home that gives you Wi-Fi. The internet comes into the house through it.

sentence.da: Jeg skal købe en ny **router**, fordi internettet er langsomt.
sentence.en: I have to buy a new router because the internet is slow.

en rude.explanation: "En rude" means "a window pane", the glass part of a window. A whole window is et vindue (a window).

sentence.da: Bolden slog en **rude** i stykker.
sentence.en: The ball broke a window pane.

en rullepølse.explanation: "En rullepølse" means "a rolled pork sausage (cold cut)", spiced pork that is rolled up, pressed and sliced thin. Despite pølse (sausage), it is eaten cold, not cooked in a pan.

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have **rullepølse** på rugbrød.
sentence.en: I would like to have rolled pork sausage on rye bread.

en rulletrappe.explanation: "En rulletrappe" means "an escalator". It is built from rulle (roll) and trappe (stairs), and the same rulle is in en rullestol (a wheelchair).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **rulletrappe** op til caféen.
sentence.en: We take an escalator up to the café.

en runde.explanation: "En runde" means "a round", one turn in a game or race: Vi spiller en runde mere (We play one more round). It also means a short walk: Vi går en runde i parken (We take a stroll in the park).

sentence.da: Vi spiller lige en **runde** mere, og så går vi.
sentence.en: We play one more round, and then we leave.

en rundkørsel.explanation: "En rundkørsel" means "a roundabout". It is built from rund (round) and kørsel (driving): Der er tre veje ind til rundkørslen (There are three roads into the roundabout).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **rundkørsel** ved stationen.
sentence.en: There is a big roundabout by the station.

en rundvisning.explanation: "En rundvisning" means "a guided tour", where a guide shows you around a place.

sentence.da: Der er en **rundvisning** på slottet klokken to.
sentence.en: There is a guided tour of the castle at two o'clock.

en rune.explanation: "En rune" means "a rune", a character from the oldest writing in Scandinavia, cut into stone or wood. A rune stone is en runesten.

sentence.da: Hver **rune** på stenen er et tegn fra vikingetiden.
sentence.en: Each rune on the stone is a sign from the Viking Age.

en russer.explanation: "En russer" means "a Russian", a person from Russia: Min nabo er russer (My neighbor is Russian). The country is Rusland (Russia), and the language is russisk (Russian).

sentence.da: Min kollega er **russer** og kommer fra Moskva.
sentence.en: My colleague is Russian and comes from Moscow.

en rute.explanation: "En rute" means "a route", the way you plan to go. Buses and trains also run on a fixed route: Bussen kører på en fast rute gennem byen (The bus runs on a fixed route through town).

sentence.da: Vi tager den korteste **rute** til byen.
sentence.en: We take the shortest route to town.

en rutine.explanation: "En rutine" means "a routine", things you do the same way each day: Jeg har en fast rutine (I have a fixed routine). It also means experience: Hun har stor rutine (She has a lot of experience).

sentence.da: Jeg har en fast **rutine** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I have a fixed routine every morning.

en rutsjebane.explanation: "En rutsjebane" means "a slide" at a playground, and also "a roller coaster" at an amusement park: Børnene elsker rutsjebanen (The children love the slide). The place tells you which one is meant.

sentence.da: Hun glider ned ad en **rutsjebane** på legepladsen.
sentence.en: She slides down a slide at the playground.

en ryg.explanation: "En ryg" means "a back", the back of your body. Danish says the back where English says my back: Jeg har ondt i ryggen (literally I have pain in the back) means "My back hurts". At ligge på ryggen means "to lie on your back".

sentence.da: Han har en bred **ryg** og stærke skuldre.
sentence.en: He has a broad back and strong shoulders.

en rygrad.explanation: "En rygrad" means "a spine", the line of bones down the middle of your back. Rygsøjle (spinal column) is the more medical word for the same thing. Rygrad also means courage: Hun har rygrad (She has backbone).

sentence.da: Din **rygrad** går fra nakken og ned til bækkenet.
sentence.en: Your spine runs from the neck down to the pelvis.

en rygsæk.explanation: "En rygsæk" means "a backpack". It is made of ryg (back) and sæk (sack), and sæk also stands alone: en sæk kartofler (a sack of potatoes).

sentence.da: Jeg bærer min **rygsæk** på ryggen.
sentence.en: I carry my backpack on my back.

en rynke.explanation: "En rynke" means "a wrinkle", a thin fold or line, most often in skin but also in cloth. At rynke panden (to frown) literally means to wrinkle the forehead.

sentence.da: Hun har en dyb **rynke** mellem øjenbrynene.
sentence.en: She has a deep wrinkle between her eyebrows.

en rysten.explanation: "En rysten" means "a shiver", a quick tremble through the body from cold, fear or excitement. It is mostly used in the singular, often with gå gennem (go through): Der gik en rysten gennem rummet (A shiver went through the room).

sentence.da: Der gik en **rysten** gennem hele kroppen.
sentence.en: A shiver went through the whole body.

en rytme.explanation: "En rytme" means "a rhythm", a pattern of sounds and pauses that repeats, in music, speech or movement. It also describes a daily pattern: dagens rytme (the rhythm of the day).

sentence.da: Trommerne giver sangen en fast **rytme**.
sentence.en: The drums give the song a steady rhythm.

en rådgiver.explanation: "En rådgiver" means "an adviser", someone whose job is to guide others with expert knowledge, for example in money, law or careers: en økonomisk rådgiver (a financial adviser).

sentence.da: Vores **rådgiver** i banken hjalp os med at vælge et lån.
sentence.en: Our adviser at the bank helped us choose a loan.

en række.explanation: "En række" means "a row" of things side by side, and also "a series": Vi sidder i første række (We sit in the front row). En række problemer means "a number of problems".

sentence.da: Vi sidder i første **række** i biografen.
sentence.en: We sit in the front row at the movie theater.

en rækkevidde.explanation: "En rækkevidde" means "a range" or "a reach", how far something can get or carry. It is used for things like a signal, a weapon or a battery: en elbils rækkevidde (an electric car's range).

sentence.da: Radioen har en lang **rækkevidde** og virker næsten overalt.
sentence.en: The radio has a long range and works almost everywhere.

en ræv.explanation: "En ræv" means "a fox", the wild red animal of forests and fields. It is also used for a sly person: Han er så snu som en ræv (He is as sly as a fox).

sentence.da: Jeg så en **ræv** løbe over marken.
sentence.en: I saw a fox run across the field.

en rødbede.explanation: "En rødbede" means "a beet", a dark red root vegetable that grows in the ground and is often eaten pickled. The name starts with rød (red).

sentence.da: Salaten er rød, fordi jeg har en **rødbede** i.
sentence.en: The salad is red because I put a beet in it.

en rødmen.explanation: "En rødmen" means "a blush", the red color that rises in your face when you feel self-conscious. The matching action is at rødme (to blush).

sentence.da: Der kom en **rødmen** på hendes kinder, fordi hun var flov.
sentence.en: A blush came onto her cheeks because she was embarrassed.

en rødspætte.explanation: "En rødspætte" means "a plaice", a flatfish with orange spots on its brown back. It is very common in Danish waters and a classic dish when fried.

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser vi stegt **rødspætte** med remoulade.
sentence.en: For lunch we eat fried plaice with remoulade.

en rødvin.explanation: "En rødvin" means "a red wine". It is made of rød (red) and vin (wine). To order, say et glas rødvin (a glass of red wine) or en flaske rødvin (a bottle of red wine).

sentence.da: **Rødvin** er lavet af mørke druer.
sentence.en: Red wine is made of dark grapes.

en røgalarm.explanation: "En røgalarm" means "a smoke alarm", a device on the ceiling that warns you about smoke with a loud beep. It is built from røg (smoke) and alarm (alarm).

sentence.da: En **røgalarm** bipper, når der er røg.
sentence.en: A smoke alarm beeps when there is smoke.

en røremaskine.explanation: "En røremaskine" means "a stand mixer", a kitchen machine that mixes dough and batter for you. It is built from røre (to stir) and maskine (machine).

sentence.da: Jeg laver kagedej i min **røremaskine**.
sentence.en: I make cake batter in my stand mixer.

en røver.explanation: "En røver" means "a robber", someone who takes things by force or threats. A tyv (thief) steals quietly, without anyone noticing.

sentence.da: En **røver** truede kassedamen og tog alle pengene.
sentence.en: A robber threatened the cashier and took all the money.

et rat.explanation: "Et rat" means "a steering wheel", the round part in front of the driver. Do not mix it up with et hjul (a wheel), which turns on the ground.

sentence.da: Man styrer bilen med et **rat**.
sentence.en: You steer the car with a steering wheel.

et realkreditlån.explanation: "Et realkreditlån" means "a mortgage", money borrowed to buy a house, where the house itself guarantees that it is paid back. It comes from a mortgage credit institution, not from an ordinary bank.

sentence.da: Huset er købt med et **realkreditlån**, som vi betaler af hver måned.
sentence.en: The house was bought with a mortgage that we pay off every month.

et reb.explanation: "Et reb" means "a rope", a thick strong cord for tying or climbing. A thinner one is en snor (a string).

sentence.da: Han bandt båden fast med et **reb**.
sentence.en: He tied up the boat with a rope.

et referat.explanation: "Et referat" means "a summary", a short written account of what was said. At a meeting it is the minutes: at skrive referat (to write the minutes). The word comes from at referere (to report).

sentence.da: Efter mødet sender hun et **referat** til alle.
sentence.en: After the meeting, she sends the minutes to everyone.

et regeringsparti.explanation: "Et regeringsparti" means "a governing party", a political party that takes part in the government. A party outside the government is called et oppositionsparti (an opposition party).

sentence.da: Et **regeringsparti** har ministre og er med til at styre landet.
sentence.en: A governing party has ministers and helps run the country.

et regnskab.explanation: "Et regnskab" means "accounts", the written record of all the money a company or person earns and spends. It is often used with at lave (to make): Han laver regnskab for firmaet (He does the accounts for the company). The accounts for a whole year are et årsregnskab (annual accounts).

sentence.da: Revisoren tjekker firmaets **regnskab**, så alle tal passer.
sentence.en: The auditor checks the company's accounts so that all the numbers add up.

et rejsebureau.explanation: "Et rejsebureau" means "a travel agency", an office that sells trips and holidays. It is built from rejse (trip) and bureau (office).

sentence.da: Vi bestiller ferien på et **rejsebureau** i byen.
sentence.en: We are booking the vacation at a travel agency in town.

et rejsekort.explanation: "Et rejsekort" means "a travel card", the Danish card for buses, trains and the metro. You tap it when you get on and again when you get off: Husk at checke ud (Remember to check out).

sentence.da: Jeg checker ind med mit **rejsekort** i bussen.
sentence.en: I check in with my travel card on the bus.

et rejsemål.explanation: "Et rejsemål" means "a destination", the place you are traveling to. The second part is mål (goal), so it is the goal of your journey.

sentence.da: Vores næste **rejsemål** er en lille by i Italien.
sentence.en: Our next destination is a small town in Italy.

et rektangel.explanation: "Et rektangel" means "a rectangle", a figure with four corners, two long sides and two short sides.

sentence.da: Skærmen på min telefon er et **rektangel**.
sentence.en: The screen on my phone is a rectangle.

et rengøringsmiddel.explanation: "Et rengøringsmiddel" means "a cleaning product", like a spray or a liquid for cleaning. It is built from rengøring (cleaning) and et middel (an agent).

sentence.da: Med et **rengøringsmiddel** kan jeg gøre badeværelset rent.
sentence.en: With a cleaning product I can clean the bathroom.

et renseri.explanation: "Et renseri" means "a dry cleaner's", a shop where you leave coats, suits and other delicate clothes to be cleaned professionally. The word comes from at rense (to clean).

sentence.da: Fordi jakken ikke tåler vand, skal den på et **renseri**.
sentence.en: Because the jacket cannot take water, it has to go to a dry cleaner's.

et repertoire.explanation: "Et repertoire" means "a repertoire", all the pieces of music or plays that a performer or theater knows well enough to perform. It also works for everyday skills: Han har et stort repertoire af vittigheder (He has a large repertoire of jokes).

sentence.da: Koret har et stort **repertoire** med både gamle og nye sange.
sentence.en: The choir has a large repertoire with both old and new songs.

et resultat.explanation: "Et resultat" means "a result", what you get at the end of a match, an exam or an experiment. In sports, it is the score: Resultatet blev 2-1 (The result was 2-1).

sentence.da: Vi fik et godt **resultat** på prøven.
sentence.en: We got a good result on the test.

et resumé.explanation: "Et resumé" means "a summary", a short retelling of the key points of a text, a book or a talk. It is not a job résumé: for that, Danish uses CV.

sentence.da: Til sidst i rapporten står et **resumé** af de vigtigste punkter.
sentence.en: At the end of the report there is a summary of the most important points.

et ribben.explanation: "Et ribben" means "a rib", one of the bones that protect your heart and lungs. In cooking, it is also a cut of pork, as in ribbensteg (a Danish roast pork dish).

sentence.da: Et **ribben** er en buet knogle på siden af brystkassen.
sentence.en: A rib is a curved bone on the side of the chest.

et ritual.explanation: "Et ritual" means "a ritual", a fixed set of actions that is repeated in the same way, in religion, at ceremonies or in daily life: Kaffen om morgenen er et ritual (The morning coffee is a ritual).

sentence.da: Et **ritual** gentages på præcis samme måde hver gang.
sentence.en: A ritual is repeated in exactly the same way every time.

et rivejern.explanation: "Et rivejern" means "a grater", used for cheese, carrots and lemon peel. The second part is jern (iron), although today most graters are made of steel.

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **rivejern** til osten.
sentence.en: I use a grater for the cheese.

et rovdyr.explanation: "Et rovdyr" means "a predator", an animal that hunts other animals for food, such as a fox or a bear. The first part, rov, means plunder, and dyr means animal.

sentence.da: Ulven er et **rovdyr**, men koen spiser kun græs.
sentence.en: The wolf is a predator, but the cow only eats grass.

et rum.explanation: "Et rum" means "a room" as a part of a building. For having enough space for something, use plads (room, space): Der er plads til os (There is room for us).

sentence.da: Der er et stort **rum** ved siden af køkkenet.
sentence.en: There is a big room next to the kitchen.

et rumfang.explanation: "Et rumfang" means "a volume", the amount of space that something takes up, measured for example in liters. For how loud a sound is, use lydstyrke (loudness) instead.

sentence.da: Beregn kassens **rumfang**, når du kender længde, bredde og højde.
sentence.en: Calculate the box's volume when you know the length, width and height.

et rumskib.explanation: "Et rumskib" means "a spaceship", built from rum (space) and et skib (a ship). Rum also means "room", so the situation tells you which one.

sentence.da: Et **rumskib** kan flyve til andre planeter.
sentence.en: A spaceship can fly to other planets.

et rumvæsen.explanation: "Et rumvæsen" means "an alien", a creature from outer space, mostly in films and stories. It is built from rum (space) and væsen (a being).

sentence.da: Et **rumvæsen** er en skabning, der kommer fra en anden planet.
sentence.en: An alien is a creature that comes from another planet.

et rundstykke.explanation: "Et rundstykke" means "a bread roll", a small round bread that Danes often eat for breakfast with butter or jam. It is built from rund (round) and stykke (piece).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser et **rundstykke** med ost.
sentence.en: I eat a bread roll with cheese.

et ry.explanation: "Et ry" means "a reputation", what a person or a place is known for. It is often used with have ry for at (to be known for): Han har ry for at være stædig (He is known for being stubborn).

sentence.da: Hotellet har fået et godt **ry**, fordi personalet er venligt.
sentence.en: The hotel has gotten a good reputation because the staff is friendly.

et rygte.explanation: "Et rygte" means "a rumor", news that people pass on without knowing if it is true: Der går et rygte om, at han stopper (There is a rumor going around that he is quitting).

sentence.da: Hun spreder et **rygte** om sin nabo.
sentence.en: She is spreading a rumor about her neighbor.

et råd.explanation: "Et råd" means "a piece of advice". Råd without et is also used for money: Jeg har ikke råd til det (I can't afford it).

sentence.da: Må jeg give dig et **råd**?
sentence.en: May I give you a piece of advice?

et rådhus.explanation: "Et rådhus" means "a town hall", where the city government works: Man kan gifte sig på rådhuset (You can get married at the town hall).

sentence.da: Det gamle **rådhus** ligger midt i byen.
sentence.en: The old town hall is in the middle of town.

et rådyr.explanation: "Et rådyr" means "a roe deer", a small, brown wild deer that lives in forests and fields. It is smaller than et krondyr (a red deer), and only the males have antlers.

sentence.da: Et **rådyr** har lange ben og kan springe højt over hegn.
sentence.en: A roe deer has long legs and can jump high over fences.

et rækkehus.explanation: "Et rækkehus" means "a townhouse" or "a row house": one of several houses built side by side in a row. It is built from række (row) and hus (house).

sentence.da: I et **rækkehus** deler man væg med naboerne.
sentence.en: In a townhouse you share a wall with the neighbors.

et røntgenbillede.explanation: "Et røntgenbillede" means "an X-ray image", a picture of the inside of the body, taken with X-rays. A doctor uses it to see a broken bone or a problem in the lungs. You say at tage et røntgenbillede (to take an X-ray).

sentence.da: Man kan se knoglerne inde i kroppen på et **røntgenbillede**.
sentence.en: You can see the bones inside the body on an X-ray.

et rør.explanation: "Et rør" means "a pipe" or "a tube", for water, gas or other things.

sentence.da: Vandet løber gennem et **rør** under gulvet.
sentence.en: The water runs through a pipe under the floor.

et røveri.explanation: "Et røveri" means "a robbery", when someone takes things by force or threats. The person who does it is en røver (a robber).

sentence.da: Der var et **røveri** i butikken i går.
sentence.en: There was a robbery in the store yesterday.

radikal.explanation: "Radikal" means "radical", for a change or idea that goes to the root of things instead of making small adjustments. In Danish it is not always negative: en radikal forbedring (a radical improvement).

sentence.da: Regeringen vil lave en **radikal** reform, som ændrer hele skattesystemet.
sentence.en: The government wants to make a radical reform that changes the whole tax system.

raps.explanation: "En raps" means "rapeseed", a crop that grows in fields and whose seeds are pressed into oil. It has no plural in everyday use.

sentence.da: Markerne bliver helt gule, når **raps** blomstrer om foråret.
sentence.en: The fields turn completely yellow when rapeseed blooms in the spring.

rar.explanation: "Rar" means "nice" or "kind", for people in a warm, everyday way. It also works for situations: Det var rart at se dig (It was nice to see you).

sentence.da: Din nabo er meget **rar**, og han hjælper os ofte.
sentence.en: Your neighbor is very nice, and he often helps us.

rasende.explanation: "Rasende" means "furious", extremely mad. It is a strong word, so for light annoyance use irriteret (annoyed): Jeg er irriteret (I am annoyed), not rasende.

sentence.da: Han var **rasende**, fordi bilen var væk.
sentence.en: He was furious because the car was gone.

rask.explanation: "Rask" means "healthy" or "well again", especially after being ill. At blive rask means "to get well". It can also mean quick and lively, as in et raskt tempo (a brisk pace).

sentence.da: Du bliver **rask** igen.
sentence.en: You will get well again.

rastløs.explanation: "Rastløs" means "restless", not able to settle or relax, in body or in mind. It is built from en rast (a break, a rest stop) and -løs (without), so it is literally "without rest".

sentence.da: Efter flere uger uden arbejde blev han **rastløs** og ville ud.
sentence.en: After several weeks without work he became restless and wanted to get out.

rationel.explanation: "Rationel" means "rational", based on logic and clear thinking. About a method it can also mean "efficient and well organized": en rationel arbejdsgang (an efficient way of working).

sentence.da: Hun er meget **rationel** og vælger altid ud fra fakta, ikke følelser.
sentence.en: She is very rational and always chooses based on facts, not feelings.

rav.explanation: "Et rav" means "amber": the golden-brown, hardened sap of ancient trees. It is polished and used for necklaces and rings.

sentence.da: Man finder ofte **rav** på stranden efter en storm.
sentence.en: You often find amber on the beach after a storm.

realistisk.explanation: "Realistisk" means "realistic", based on how things really are. It is used about plans and goals that can actually be reached, and about paintings or films that look like real life.

sentence.da: Det er ikke **realistisk** at nå hele vejen på en time.
sentence.en: It is not realistic to make it the whole way in an hour.

regelmæssigt.explanation: "Regelmæssigt" means "regularly", happening again and again at steady, predictable times. It is not the same as ofte (often): you can do something often but not regularly if there is no fixed pattern.

sentence.da: Du skal motionere **regelmæssigt**, hvis du vil blive stærkere.
sentence.en: You must exercise regularly if you want to become stronger.

registreret.explanation: "Registreret" means "registered", written into an official list or system, for people, companies, vehicles and cases. For a registered letter in the mail, Danes say et anbefalet brev instead.

sentence.da: Bilen er **registreret** i Danmark, så den har danske nummerplader.
sentence.en: The car is registered in Denmark, so it has Danish license plates.

regn.explanation: "Regn" means "rain", the weather itself. To say that it is raining, use Det regner (It is raining), not Det er regn.

sentence.da: Der kommer meget **regn** i dag.
sentence.en: A lot of rain is coming today.

regnfuld.explanation: "Regnfuld" means "rainy", for a day, week or season with a lot of rain. It is built from regn (rain) and -fuld (full of), as in fredfuld (peaceful).

sentence.da: Det blev en **regnfuld** sommer, så vi var mest indendørs.
sentence.en: It became a rainy summer, so we were mostly indoors.

regnfuldt.explanation: "Regnfuldt" means "rainy", for weather and days with a lot of rain. To say it is raining right now, use Det regner (It is raining).

sentence.da: Vejret har været **regnfuldt** hele ugen.
sentence.en: The weather has been rainy all week.

regntøj.explanation: "Regntøj" means "rain gear", the waterproof clothes you wear in rainy weather. It covers a whole outfit, so there is no plural.

sentence.da: Børnene har **regntøj** på, fordi det regner.
sentence.en: The children are wearing rain gear because it is raining.

regnvejr.explanation: "Regnvejr" means "rainy weather". It is built from regn (rain) and vejr (weather). For rain falling right now, Danish uses a verb: Det regner (It is raining).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en paraply med i **regnvejr**.
sentence.en: I bring an umbrella in rainy weather.

rejer.explanation: "Rejer" means "shrimp" or "prawns", and this plural is the form you mostly hear. En rejemad (a shrimp sandwich) is built from reje (shrimp) and mad (food).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser gerne fisk og **rejer** fra havet.
sentence.en: I like eating fish and shrimp from the sea.

relativt.explanation: "Relativt" means "relatively", placed before a word to say it is so compared with what is normal. It is softer than meget (very): relativt dyr (fairly expensive) is less strong than meget dyr (very expensive).

sentence.da: Prisen er **relativt** lav, når man tænker på kvaliteten.
sentence.en: The price is relatively low when you think about the quality.

relevant.explanation: "Relevant" means "relevant", for something that fits the topic and matters in the situation. It is often said about questions, facts and information: Det er ikke relevant (That is not relevant).

sentence.da: Dit spørgsmål er **relevant**, men vi har ikke tid.
sentence.en: Your question is relevant, but we do not have time.

religiøs.explanation: "Religiøs" means "religious", about faith and its practices, for people and for things like holidays, music and symbols. For a person, Danes also say troende (a believer): Hun er troende (She is a believer).

sentence.da: Jul er en **religiøs** højtid for kristne, men mange fejrer den alligevel.
sentence.en: Christmas is a religious holiday for Christians, but many celebrate it anyway.

remoulade.explanation: "Remoulade" means "remoulade", a creamy Danish sauce. It is typically eaten with fried fish or on hot dogs.

sentence.da: **Remoulade** er en kold sauce med små agurker.
sentence.en: Remoulade is a cold sauce with small pickles.

ren.explanation: "Ren" means "clean" and also "pure": rent vand (pure water), rent guld (pure gold). At gøre rent means "to clean" a home or room.

sentence.da: Luften i skoven er **ren**.
sentence.en: The air in the forest is clean.

reserveret.explanation: "Reserveret" means "reserved" and comes from at reservere (to reserve). It also describes people: a reserveret person is reserved, meaning a little distant and keeping to themselves.

sentence.da: Bordet er **reserveret** til os.
sentence.en: The table is reserved for us.

respekt.explanation: "Respekt" means "respect", both admiration and polite behavior toward others: Han har stor respekt for sin chef (He has great respect for his boss).

sentence.da: Børn skal lære at vise **respekt** for ældre.
sentence.en: Children must learn to show respect for older people.

resten.explanation: "Resten" means "the rest", what remains after you take a part. It is often followed by af (of) and then what the rest is of.

sentence.da: Du kan få **resten** af kagen.
sentence.en: You can have the rest of the cake.

rester.explanation: "Rester" means "leftovers", food from an earlier meal. The single word en rest means "a remainder", as in resten af kagen (the rest of the cake).

forms.en: There are leftovers in the fridge.
We do not have many leftovers.

sentence.da: I dag spiser vi **rester** fra middagen i går.
sentence.en: Today we eat leftovers from yesterday's dinner.

retfærdig.explanation: "Retfærdig" means "fair" or "just", for decisions, people and punishments that treat everyone as they deserve. The opposite is uretfærdig (unfair). In everyday talk, Danes also use fair itself: Det er ikke fair (That is not fair).

sentence.da: Læreren er **retfærdig** og giver alle de samme chancer.
sentence.en: The teacher is fair and gives everyone the same chances.

retfærdighed.explanation: "En retfærdighed" means "justice", the idea that people are treated fairly and get what they deserve. It is the word that goes with retfærdig (fair), and it is mostly used without en: Der skal være retfærdighed (There must be justice).

sentence.da: **Retfærdighed** betyder, at alle behandles ens.
sentence.en: Justice means that everyone is treated equally.

retskrivning.explanation: "En retskrivning" means "spelling rules": the official rules for how words are written. It is built from ret (correct) and skrivning (writing). In Denmark, Dansk Sprognævn (the Danish Language Council) sets the rules and publishes them in Retskrivningsordbogen (the official dictionary).

sentence.da: Reglerne i dansk **retskrivning** hjælper os med at stave rigtigt.
sentence.en: The rules of Danish spelling help us spell correctly.

retssikkerhed.explanation: "En retssikkerhed" means "legal certainty": the protection that makes sure everyone is treated by the same fair rules and can defend themselves. It is built from rets (of the law) and sikkerhed (security).

related.en: a state under the rule of law

sentence.da: Uden **retssikkerhed** kan man blive straffet uden en fair rettergang.
