sentence.en: Without legal certainty, you can be punished without a fair trial.

ridning.explanation: "Ridning" means "horse riding", the sport or hobby. A single outing is called en ridetur (a ride): Vi tog på en ridetur (We went on a ride). It is built on at ride (to ride).

sentence.da: Til **ridning** skal man bruge en hest og en hjelm.
sentence.en: For horse riding you need a horse and a helmet.

rig.explanation: "Rig" means "rich", having a lot of money, but it also means rich in other things: rig på erfaring (rich in experience). Do not mix it up with et rige (a kingdom), which looks almost the same.

sentence.da: Han er meget **rig** og har mange penge.
sentence.en: He is very rich and has a lot of money.

rigdom.explanation: "En rigdom" means "wealth": a large amount of money or valuable things. It can also be about things that are not money: en rigdom af detaljer (a wealth of details).

sentence.da: Landets **rigdom** kommer fra olie og fiskeri.
sentence.en: The country's wealth comes from oil and fishing.

rigeligt.explanation: "Rigeligt" means "plenty", more than needed. It is also a polite answer when you are offered more: Mere kaffe? Nej tak, jeg har rigeligt (More coffee? No thanks, I have plenty).

sentence.da: Vi har **rigeligt** med mad, så alle kan blive mætte.
sentence.en: We have plenty of food, so everyone can get full.

rigtig.explanation: "Rigtig" means "correct" or "right". It also means "real" or "proper". In casual speech it can mean "really": rigtig god (really good).

sentence.da: Ja, din løsning er **rigtig**!
sentence.en: Yes, your solution is correct!

rimelig.explanation: "Rimelig" means "reasonable" and "fair". About a price, it means not too expensive. About a situation, it means fair: Det er ikke rimeligt (That is not fair).

sentence.da: Prisen på hotellet er **rimelig**, og værelset er stort.
sentence.en: The price of the hotel is reasonable, and the room is big.

ris.explanation: "Ris" means "rice", the small grains you boil as a side dish.

sentence.da: Jeg koger **ris** og laver kylling til aftensmad.
sentence.en: I boil rice and make chicken for dinner.

risengrød.explanation: "En risengrød" means "rice porridge", rice cooked slowly in milk and eaten warm. It is a meal, not a dessert. The cold dessert made from it at Christmas is risalamande (cold rice pudding with almonds and cherry sauce).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser vi **risengrød** med smør, sukker og kanel.
sentence.en: For lunch we eat rice porridge with butter, sugar and cinnamon.

risikabel.explanation: "Risikabel" means "risky", with a real chance that something goes wrong or is lost. It is about a choice or plan, while farlig (dangerous) is about things that can hurt you.

sentence.da: Det er en **risikabel** plan, for vi kan miste alle pengene.
sentence.en: It is a risky plan, because we could lose all the money.

ro.explanation: "Ro" means "calm" and "peace and quiet", something you can have or find. To tell someone to relax, say Slap af (Relax).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have **ro**, når jeg læser.
sentence.en: I would like some peace and quiet when I read.

robust.explanation: "Robust" means "robust", able to take hard use without breaking or getting ill. It is used for objects and materials, and for a person who does not get sick or upset easily.

sentence.da: Telefonen er **robust**, så den kan tåle et fald.
sentence.en: The phone is robust, so it can survive a fall.

rock.explanation: "Rock" means "rock" as in music. The stone is en sten (a stone), not rock.

sentence.da: Jeg elsker **rock** med høje guitarer og trommer.
sentence.en: I love rock with loud guitars and drums.

rodet.explanation: "Rodet" means "messy", for a room or desk with things lying around. It is not about dirt: Rummet er rodet, men ikke snavset (The room is messy, but not dirty).

sentence.da: Børneværelset er meget **rodet** i dag.
sentence.en: The children's room is very messy today.

rolig.explanation: "Rolig" means "calm" or "relaxed", and "peaceful" or "quiet" for places. Vær rolig means "Stay calm" or "Calm down". Roligt also means "calmly": Tal roligt (Speak calmly).

sentence.da: Peter er helt **rolig** og smiler.
sentence.en: Peter is completely calm and smiling.

romantik.explanation: "Romantik" means "romance", the feeling of love and closeness between two people. It often shows up in a negative: Der er ikke meget romantik i at vaske op (There is not much romance in doing the dishes).

sentence.da: Levende lys og blomster giver **romantik**.
sentence.en: Candles and flowers bring romance.

romantisk.explanation: "Romantisk" means "romantic", for love and dreamy moments: en romantisk middag (a romantic dinner).

sentence.da: Det er **romantisk** at gå en tur ved havet.
sentence.en: It is romantic to go for a walk by the sea.

roning.explanation: "Roning" means "rowing", the sport of moving a boat forward with your own muscle power. Rowers sit facing backward, which is the main difference from paddling.

forms.en: to do rowing (as a club sport)

sentence.da: Til **roning** bruger man årer og sin egen muskelkraft.
sentence.en: For rowing you use oars and your own muscle power.

ros.explanation: "Ros" means "praise", words that tell someone they did well: Eleven fik ros fra læreren (The student got praise from the teacher).

sentence.da: Hun fik meget **ros** for sit arbejde.
sentence.en: She got a lot of praise for her work.

rug.explanation: "En rug" means "rye", a cereal crop grown for its flour. Danes use it above all for the dark bread called rugbrød (rye bread).

sentence.da: Mel af **rug** gør brødet mørkt og tungt.
sentence.en: Flour made from rye makes the bread dark and heavy.

rugbrød.explanation: "Rugbrød" means "rye bread", a dark, heavy bread. It is made of rug (rye) and brød (bread). It is the usual base for smørrebrød (open sandwiches).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger ost på en skive **rugbrød**.
sentence.en: I put cheese on a slice of rye bread.

rummelig.explanation: "Rummelig" means "spacious", with a lot of room inside, for a room, a car or a cupboard. It is built on et rum (a room, a space).

sentence.da: Bilen er **rummelig**, og der er plads til hele familien.
sentence.en: The car is spacious, and there is room for the whole family.

rund.explanation: "Rund" means "round", for a shape. It is also used for round numbers: runde tal (round numbers) are numbers like 10 and 100.

sentence.da: Jorden er **rund**, ikke flad.
sentence.en: The earth is round, not flat.

rundt om hjørnet.explanation: "Rundt om hjørnet" means "around the corner". It can be a place: Posthuset ligger rundt om hjørnet (The post office is around the corner). It can also be a time: Julen er lige rundt om hjørnet (Christmas is just around the corner).

forms.en: The bakery is around the corner.

forms.da: Butikken er lige rundt om hjørnet.
forms.en: The shop is just around the corner.

sentence.da: Banken ligger lige **rundt om hjørnet**.
sentence.en: The bank is just around the corner.

rusland.explanation: "Rusland" means "Russia". Compare Jeg bor i Rusland (I live in Russia) with Jeg rejser til Rusland (I am traveling to Russia).

sentence.da: Man taler russisk i **Rusland**.
sentence.en: People speak Russian in Russia.

russisk.explanation: "Russisk" means "Russian", for the language and for things from Russia: Jeg taler lidt russisk (I speak a little Russian).

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Rusland og taler **russisk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Russia and speaks Russian.

ryddelig.explanation: "Ryddelig" means "tidy", with everything in its place. It is the result of at rydde op (to tidy up), where op works like up in English.

sentence.da: Hendes lejlighed er altid **ryddelig** og pæn.
sentence.en: Her apartment is always tidy and nice.

rynket.explanation: "Rynket" means "wrinkled", with small folds or lines in a surface, for skin and clothes. It comes from at rynke (to wrinkle): at rynke panden is to frown (to wrinkle the forehead).

sentence.da: Skjorten er helt **rynket**, så jeg må stryge den.
sentence.en: The shirt is all wrinkled, so I have to iron it.

rystende.explanation: "Rystende" means "shocking": so upsetting that it shakes you. It comes from at ryste (to shake), and it can also mean literally shaking, as in rystende hænder (trembling hands).

sentence.da: Billederne fra ulykken var **rystende**, og mange græd.
sentence.en: The pictures from the accident were shocking, and many cried.

rystet.explanation: "Rystet" means "shaken", deeply troubled after a shock such as an accident or bad news. It comes from at ryste (to shake), but here it describes your inner state.

sentence.da: Hun var meget **rystet** efter den alvorlige ulykke på motorvejen.
sentence.en: She was very shaken after the serious accident on the highway.

rå.explanation: "Rå" means "raw" for food. It also means "crude" or "rough" for words and behavior: et råt sprog (rough language).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke lide **rå** løg.
sentence.en: I do not like raw onions.

rædselsslagen.explanation: "Rædselsslagen" means "terrified", very strongly afraid. It is built from en rædsel (a horror) and slagen (struck), so it is literally "struck by horror". It is much stronger than bange (afraid).

sentence.da: Hun blev **rædselsslagen**, da hun så slangen på gulvet.
sentence.en: She became terrified when she saw the snake on the floor.

rød.explanation: "Rød" means "red". It is part of words like rødvin (red wine) and rødbede (beet).

sentence.da: Tomaten er **rød**.
sentence.en: The tomato is red.

rødgrød.explanation: "En rødgrød" means "red berry pudding", a thick dessert of cooked red berries, eaten cold with cream. Despite the ending grød (porridge), it has no grain in it: it is thickened berry juice.

forms.en: a bowl of red berry pudding

sentence.da: Til dessert fik vi kold **rødgrød** med fløde.
sentence.en: For dessert we had cold red berry pudding with cream.

rødhåret.explanation: "Rødhåret" means "red-haired", with red or ginger hair. Many hair words are built the same way, from a color or a quality plus hår (hair): lyshåret (fair-haired), mørkhåret (dark-haired), gråhåret (gray-haired).

sentence.da: Min lillesøster er **rødhåret**, og hendes hår er næsten orange.
sentence.en: My little sister is red-haired, and her hair is almost orange.

røg.explanation: "Røg" means "smoke", the gray cloud that comes from burning things, such as a cigarette.

forms.en: There is smoke in the room.

sentence.da: Jeg kan se **røg** fra skorstenen.
sentence.en: I can see smoke from the chimney.

rørende.explanation: "Rørende" means "touching" or "moving", which makes you feel warm or tearful. It comes from at røre (to touch, to stir). How you feel is rørt (moved): Jeg blev rørt (I was moved).

sentence.da: Talen var **rørende**, og flere i salen græd.
sentence.en: The speech was touching, and several people in the hall cried.

rørsukker.explanation: "Rørsukker" means "cane sugar", sugar made from sugarcane. Sugar in Danish shops usually comes from sugar beets instead. The word is built on et rør (a reed, a cane) and sukker (sugar).

sentence.da: **Rørsukker** laves af planten sukkerrør, som vokser i varme lande.
sentence.en: Cane sugar is made from the plant sugarcane, which grows in warm countries.

rørt.explanation: "Rørt" means "touched" and describes being moved by a warm or sad moment: Jeg blev rørt over hendes ord (I was touched by her words). It is not about touching something with your hand.

sentence.da: Jeg blev så **rørt** over din gave.
sentence.en: I was so touched by your gift.

røræg.explanation: "Røræg" means "scrambled eggs". It comes from at røre (to stir) and æg (egg), because you stir the eggs while they cook. Compare et spejlæg (a fried egg), which stays whole.

sentence.da: Vi laver **røræg** med bacon til morgenmad.
sentence.en: We make scrambled eggs with bacon for breakfast.
